chapters.title: Slowly Drawing Closer
chapters.content:
"Stop overthinking. Go to sleep."

Sensing that the woman beside him was lost in thought, Zhao Xuanyou patted her head and gently kissed her forehead.

After spending half the day drinking outside, he was now tired and wanted to hold her and sleep early.

"Mmm."

Warm breath brushed against his face, carrying a hint of alcohol.

If she wanted to change her status, Yu Wan would have to become Zhao Xuanyou's concubine, but Zhao Xuanyou seemed quite devoted to Cui Yichu.

She couldn't push herself too much; excess would only backfire and make Zhao Xuanyou dislike her.

He didn't have strong feelings for "Yu Wan." If she and Cui Yichu had a falling out right now, he would still side with Cui Yichu.

Yu Wan turned over, facing away from him, avoiding the alcohol on his body. After a moment of irritation, she fell into a deep sleep.

The next morning, Baozhu came in to wake her as usual.

In the main house, Cui Yichu had finished her toilette and ordered the maids to prepare breakfast. By the time Zhao Xuanyou got up, the warm pavilion was already set with small dishes and fragrant congee.

Cui Yichu usually ate light, but to suit Zhao Xuanyou's taste, she had specially added a dish of scallion oil chicken, a steamer of shiitake and pork buns, and a plate of pickled duck.

Even Zhao Xuanyou, who was used to simplicity outside, found this thoughtful preparation comfortable.

After the couple finished their meal, they rested in the warm pavilion for a while. Baozhu then served rose dew, and the two each drank a cup, sweet and refreshing, just right.

After setting down her cup, Cui Yichu softly asked, "Will the Heir be going out today?"

Zhao Xuanyou nodded but didn't elaborate as he had before.

Cui Yichu didn't dare to press further. After paying their respects to Lady Ye together, they parted ways; Cui Yichu returned to Liu Fang Hall, and Zhao Xuanyou went to Honghui Hall.

He changed into a formal outfit, and when he stepped out, he saw Yu Wan busy in the courtyard.

The courtyard was clean, the morning light just rising. Yu Wan wore a seasonally appropriate blue dress, her waist cinched with an embroidered sash, making her figure look slender and graceful.

Though her figure was graceful, she was still young, her eyes and brows full of youthful charm.

"Heir."

Yu Wan saw him come out and curtsied to him.

Today, Zhao Xuanyou was dressed quite formally, in brocade robes and jade belt, elegant and refined, exuding an air of nobility.

It seemed he wasn't going out to meet friends but to pay a visit to someone important.

Zhao Xuanyou paused for a moment, suddenly recalling what his wife had said last night about considering elevating Yu Wan to a concubine.

She was indeed extremely beautiful, unmatched by anyone.

However, Zhao Xuanyou truly had no intention of taking her in.

He withdrew his gaze and walked straight out.

Yu Wan watched him grow distant, feeling a sense of helplessness. This man was so devoted to Cui Yichu that unless Cui Yichu spoke up, it would be hard to shake his resolve.

For now, she could only slowly draw closer, letting him gradually accept her presence.

"What are you staring at?" Yuan Qing unknowingly stood beside Yu Wan.

Yu Wan quickly averted her gaze and continued arranging the flowers in her hands. "Nothing."

"You were looking at the Heir."

Hearing Yuan Qing say this so certainly, Yu Wan didn't deny it. Instead, she smiled, "So what if I was?"

"You wouldn't be admiring the Heir, would you?"

Yu Wan pressed her lips together. "I won't tell you."

"I advise you not to have such ideas. The Heir likes the Madam so much that he doesn't even glance at other women. You were there yesterday when Miss Fengchang came, and the Heir didn't even look at her," Yuan Qing said, then suddenly blinked. "But..."

"But what?" Yu Wan pressed.

Yuan Qing was Zhao Xuanyou's close attendant and should know many things about him.

"I won't tell you either."

In truth, Yuan Qing felt that Yu Wan seemed to hold a special place in Zhao Xuanyou's heart.

He had no evidence, but he was certain that if the maid in the courtyard had been anyone else, the Heir wouldn't have paused.

Perhaps it was because Yu Wan resembled the Madam, so the Heir, out of love for his wife, paid her a little more attention.

Seeing that he wouldn't speak, Yu Wan didn't press further and seriously went back to work.

Zhao Xuanyou left the Marquis's residence and mounted his horse, heading straight for the palace gates.

After informing the palace guards, he stood quietly to one side, waiting. After about the time it takes for a stick of incense to burn, a eunuch emerged from the palace, leading Zhao Xuanyou inside. Soon, they arrived at Yangxin Hall.

The hall was resplendent with gold and jade, and auspicious beasts exhaled fragrant incense.

But Zhao Xuanyou was not visiting for the first time, so he remained calm and composed.

"Your subject Zhao Xuanyou kowtows to Your Majesty. May our Emperor live ten thousand years, ten thousand years, a hundred thousand years."

The Emperor was forty-seven this year, around the same age as the Marquis of Jingyuan. Seeing Zhao Xuanyou arrive, he set down the memorial in his hand and looked at Zhao Xuanyou kneeling before him.

"Rise and speak."

"Thank you, Your Majesty."

Zhao Xuanyou currently commanded a military region and was an important minister of the court.

This time he returned to the capital, he was on leave, not to report to the court, so he had not attended court to see the Emperor.

Yesterday, he received a secret summons from the palace and came to pay his respects early in the morning.

The Emperor asked about the border defenses, and Zhao Xuanyou answered each question with composure.

Having led troops in battle since his early teens and tempered himself on the frontier for several years, he had experienced countless life-and-death situations and storms, forging a noble and strategic demeanor.

The Emperor sat behind the imperial desk, slightly narrowing his eyes as he scrutinized Zhao Xuanyou. After a long while, he finally smiled.

"With you in the northwest, I can rest easy. You have worked hard guarding the border. The Imperial Weaving Workshop has just presented a batch of new satin. Choose five bolts to take back to your residence."

"Your subject thanks Your Majesty for your great favor."

After expressing his gratitude, Zhao Xuanyou understood that the previous words were just pleasantries, and what followed was what the Emperor truly wanted to say.

"I heard from Prince Ping that you want to stay in the capital?"

After his wife had begged him on the bed to stay in the capital, he had expressed his intention to Prince Ping. Now that the Emperor knew, it seemed Prince Ping had not brushed him off and had indeed pushed the matter forward.

Zhao Xuanyou stood upright, his posture as steadfast as a green pine.

"Your subject has been away from the capital for nearly ten years since joining the army. My father is recovering from injuries abroad and has also been away from the capital for a long time. My grandmother is advanced in years and has been in poor health lately. Now that the world is at peace and there are no wars, as a grandson, your subject should stay by his grandmother's side to fulfill his filial duties."

This speech was flawless, both praising the Emperor's peaceful reign and providing a valid reason for wanting to stay in the capital to fulfill his filial duties.

The Emperor looked at Zhao Xuanyou and nodded slightly.

"Years ago, when your father brought you into the palace, you were still a naive young boy. Now, after your experiences on the frontier, you have truly taken after your father."

"Your Majesty flatters me."

At this point, the Emperor narrowed his eyes. "There happens to be a vacancy in the Ministry of War at the rank of Langzhong, which is equivalent to your current rank."

In this dynasty, civil officials were valued over military ones. Although Zhao Xuanyou commanded a military region, apart from being the heir of the Marquis of Jingyuan, he was only a fifth-rank general.

A Langzhong in the Ministry of War was also fifth-rank, so it was indeed equivalent.

"Your subject thanks..."

"There's no need to thank me. Although you are a fifth-rank military officer, your meritorious service is outstanding. Serving as a fifth-rank official in the capital would be a waste of your talents." The Emperor pondered for a moment. "There is a vacancy for a military advisor in the Secretariat. That would be a more suitable position for you."

A military advisor in the Secretariat was a fourth-rank official. This was not only staying in the capital but also a promotion.

Zhao Xuanyou declined, "Your subject has never served as a civil official. Being granted the position of Langzhong is already a great imperial favor."

The Emperor smiled, "You may not have served as a civil official, but you are no worse than any civil official in the court. Alright, accept my decree and withdraw."

"Your subject obeys the decree and thanks Your Majesty."

Zhao Xuanyou respectfully withdrew. With the Emperor's decree, a young eunuch led him to the Imperial Household Department to receive his reward.

At the Imperial Household Department, since the Emperor had said to let Zhao Xuanyou choose for himself, the eunuch in charge, following the decree, brought out all the bolts for Zhao Xuanyou to choose from.

Zhao Xuanyou had never paid much attention to fabrics. He first picked two bolts of steady colors for his grandmother. The remaining three were all brightly colored, and just as he was about to leave, a sharp and arrogant voice suddenly came from behind him.

"There are only twenty bolts of floral satin in total. Who are you to take so many?"
